title: Bidirectional A* on London: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: See how Bidirectional A* finds the shortest path faster by searching from both start and goal until the frontiers meet. This real-map visualization mirrors how routing AI powers autonomous vehicle navigation under tight time limits.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — How autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

You’re watching Bidirectional A* slice the search space in half: one A* runs forward from the start, another runs backward from the goal. Each uses a heuristic to prioritize promising nodes, then the two waves converge—often reducing expansions dramatically vs. classic A*.

Here’s the mental model:
1) Forward search: start → …
2) Backward search: goal → …
3) Stop early when frontiers meet, reconstructing the optimal route.

Takeaway: fewer explored nodes = faster paths—exactly what time-sensitive GPS and routing systems need.

Debate question: Should routing prioritize fastest arrival, or “robust” routes that avoid uncertainty spikes (construction, traffic)?
